clinician.trajectory_summary: The patient presented with a long history of multi-systemic symptoms, including progressive musculoskeletal complaints and widespread pigmentations, evolving over several decades. The diagnosis of Alkaptonuria was conclusively established in his early 70s, following the intraoperative observation of black discolouration in bone tissue in his monozygotic twin brother (E006). This observation prompted a diagnostic triad that included a urine spot test for homogentisic acid (HGA) in both brothers (E007) and genetic DNA testing of the twin brother, which revealed heterozygous pathogenic variants in the HGD gene: c.481G>A, p.(Gly161Arg) and c.1017G>T, p.(Met339Ile). Supporting clinical evidence included the onset of pigmentation of the sclera, ears, and fingers in both brothers in their early 40s (E002), and progressive musculoskeletal symptoms starting with knee problems in his 50s, later extending to diffuse lower back, groin, and hip pain (E005).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Diagnosis was conclusively established through a diagnostic triad, including a urine spot test for HGA in both brothers.
Genetic DNA testing of the twin brother revealed a heterozygous pathogenic variant in the two genes c.481G>A, p.(Gly161Arg) and c.1017G>T, p.(Met339Ile).
Intraoperative observation of black discolouration in bone tissue in the twin brother prompted the termination of a surgical procedure and contributed to the diagnosis.
Pigmentation of the sclera, ears, and fingers began to appear in both brothers in their early 40s.
Musculoskeletal symptoms progressed from knee problems in his 50s to include diffuse lower back pain and eventually extending to encompass pain in the groin and hips.
